flags.quote: US and EU labelling rules allow the components of a fragrance mixture to be listed under the single word 'fragrance' or 'parfum'. Only specified allergens must be named individually in the EU.

substances.note: The word covers a mixture whose components are not shown on the label. Some are declared separately when they are on the EU allergen list.

flags.quote: Detergent labels may name ingredient classes (for example 'anionic surfactants 5-15%') rather than individual substances; the EU Detergents Regulation requires preservatives and listed allergens to be named individually.

substances.note: A class name tells you the type of ingredient, not which substance it is.

substances.note: The label does not show 1,4-dioxane because it is a contaminant, not an ingredient. Brands can disclose test results through the claim portal.

flags.quote: Regulation (EU) 2023/2055 (REACH Annex XVII entry 78) restricts intentionally added synthetic polymer microparticles.
